title: In 94 UK Biobank traits, regulatory elements without mammal conservation hold few extra causal variants, and their size relative to conserved DNA depends on which conserved DNA is the yardstick
abstract:
Human regulatory DNA that has no base conserved across mammals holds few extra variants that cause differences in complex traits: per variant it is 1.7 times as likely as non-conserved DNA outside regulatory elements to hold a high-confidence causal variant, less than any class of conserved non-coding DNA (3 to 40 times). This matters because biochemical activity in such DNA is often taken as evidence of function.

We used public fine-mapping results (SuSiE and FINEMAP) for 94 UK Biobank traits and for gene expression (eQTLs) in 49 GTEx tissues. The primary causal set had a posterior inclusion probability (PIP) of at least 0.9 in both methods (1,190 non-coding SNVs for traits, 11,040 for eQTLs; background PIP < 0.01). Classes were Zoonomia 241-mammal conserved bases (phyloP >= 2.27), split by phyloP and by overlap with ENCODE V4 candidate regulatory elements (cCREs), and cCREs grouped by the conservation tier of a previous SCI study (tier 0: no conserved base among assessable bases). A binomial model gave odds ratios (OR) adjusted for repeat type, allele frequency, distance to a transcription start site and gene context, with a 1-Mb block bootstrap.

Tier-0 cCREs had trait OR 1.66 (95% CI 1.19-2.14). Conserved bases had OR 40 (inside cCREs, phyloP >= 4), 12.5 (inside, phyloP 2.27-4), 11.9 (outside, phyloP >= 4) and 3.0 (outside, phyloP 2.27-4). Trait enrichment rose 3-4 times per step in conservation level and about 3 times (2.1-4.7) from outside to inside cCREs at equal conservation, while the singleton selection signal of the previous study changes by at most 1.5 times over the same contrasts. So the conserved-equivalent fraction (CEF: excess of a class divided by the excess of a conserved yardstick) of tier-0 cCREs for traits ranged from 1.7% to 34% with the yardstick. The selection CEF (1.5-1.9%) matches only the most conserved yardsticks and differs 8- to 11-fold with the selection study's own yardstick. For eQTLs, conserved DNA was much less enriched, as Kuderna et al. (2024) showed with the same data.

So non-conserved regulatory DNA adds few causal trait variants, in line with its weak selection, but no single conserved-equivalent amount describes it. Limits: the yardstick dependence was found by independent review; results depend on the PIP threshold; traits are mostly blood measures; only common and low-frequency SNVs.

citations.reason: We use its conservation tier of every ENCODE V4 cCRE and compare our trait and eQTL estimates with its selection estimates (conserved-equivalent fractions). Trait estimates agree with its tier-0 and tier-1 results only for some conserved yardsticks; we also use its inside/outside selection ratios and its phyloP gradient.
CRISPRi-validated enhancers were conserved more often if the target gene is dosage sensitive; our LOEUF analysis of eQTLs shows a related pattern with natural variants.
Transposon copies with regulatory marks showed no extra selection; tier-0 cCRE bases in transposons carry few causal trait variants here.
